### 2026-10-08 – Today, I started working on Starbie for the first time! (I wanted to get started earlier in the week, but I barely had any time). Today, I completed all the steps up to creating the ESP32 C3, as descr

**1.5h**

Today, I started working on Starbie for the first time! (I wanted to get started earlier in the week, but I barely had any time). Today, I completed all the steps up to creating the ESP32 C3, as described in the image.

A big reason I spent so much time on so few steps is that getting started (setting things up, I mean) took me a lot of time.

Even when trying to download KiCad, I was faced with immediate problems, which took me almost 20 minutes to navigate to AND to clear my treasured, high-storage downloads.

I tried to download the Week 1 Care Package, but it kept taking me to a GitHub Dev site... (the red code high-key terrified me)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/28c3ac05bbefa97ef56e055a16d815c6c0708af7234fef8cf82b5ff1524cc5d6.png)

Then, I tried to unzip the Week 1 Care Package.zip file, but my Mac wouldn't even let me do that!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/9fb246f9d2fb642da3708a447f8b37e6af20977c8f15d947cf6d49660da39443.png)

I had to research on Reddit, YouTube, and Google on how to open the .zip file without downloading an external app. I eventually ended up just redownloading it. Then, I began working on the actual components in the Schematic Editor. By this point, my brain was fried, and my computer was overloaded. I put the ESP32 C2 together with ease... then I moved on to the next step, adding the buttons, but the left-hand-side tiny green wire wasn't connecting to the label.
After further frustrating research, I realized... I wasn't even in the Schematic Editor canvas where I'm supposed to build my circuits in the first place!!! I was in the Symbol Editor layout! (according to a highly confident Google Gemini, which I was using to help me troubleshoot my various problems — see below.)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/f09501d5ab43725721f7b7052e17ccc00a4254f5a2478d93bac7838388bb23a3.png)

All in all? Objectively, I might "not have done a lot" with my 90 minutes of work time today. However, to me, my work is a massive win! I explored KiCad for the first time, learned about .sym and .pretty files for the first time (I found the ending .pretty to be super cute!), and worked in the Schematic Editor, which is a more advanced editing platform than I've ever seen before!

### 2026-10-09 – Today, I finished all five of the components up! I also moved my design from the Schematic Editor to the PCB Editor!

**3h**

Today, I finished all five of the components up! I also moved my design from the Schematic Editor to the PCB Editor!
Evidence:

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 at 7.52.53 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/8103f70db86808dfb3a72f579e7f4eb7f2ae3528a61c30e612d923aa42abba55.jpg)

Today's work session was really fun; I learned a lot about Schematic Editor, PCB Editor, how the two editors connect, and about assigning footprints!

I was able to put all of my components together much faster!! I got the hang of where to find parts and what each part meant. Learning about what each part means and how they all come together was really interesting!

Even though I ran into a few minor problems on the way, some quick research and troubleshooting with AI, as well as my own newfound, increasing understanding of Schematic Editor, helped me solve them quickly. One example was when I was confused about why my SW_Push button wasn't wiring to my label:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/e52d9ff429d3b26624af3627fb22d7f571845b4436719467760880e11233fdaf.png)

Reflecting on my feelings when creating the components, I felt a lot more confidence as I was able to put them together, especially the last two components (MPU6050 and the Environment Sensor)!

However, later on, I ran into a big problem. I had to spend almost 30 minutes figuring out why there were 4 errors when I was trying to move the design from the Schematic Editor to the PCB Editor... turned out that I accidentally assigned a footprint J2 with 1x04 pins instead of matching it with the 1x08!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/899c7131c2511a80a94cdd40db190364e345cb63cbe19691c21cb61cbc045e09.png)

 I fixed that and got to the mixed-up PCB page, which is where I left off for tonight. I have a busy day tomorrow, but I plan on spending at least a couple hours of my day arranging the components into a star shape, adding the star outline, checking for errors, and CUSTOMIZING!!!

Side note: To me, the background of the PCB Editor kind of looks like outer space!! :D

### 2026-10-11 – Today, I rearranged my components to make my star, meticulously outlined my star, and started routing my PCB.  I also installed Arduino and completed steps 1-6 of Upload with Arduino IDE in the guide.

**4h**

Today, I rearranged my components to make my star, meticulously outlined my star, and started routing my PCB.  I also installed Arduino and completed steps 1-6 of Upload with Arduino IDE in the guide.
Routing my PCB got really complicated and confusing. I'll detail it furthur below. So, I took a break from that for today, and started working on my Firmware instead.

I didn't have too many problems when I was rearranging the components (just had to click R a bunch of times to rotate them, haha). Here's me stuck after clicking R once or twice, confused as to why  I could not get my U1 and R1 to match the image:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/d9f690fdb05a7ad56bf589560ba0ff460f4b93bdf83f9f1847f813815d9f56a5.png)

Later, after mapping my star out line-by-line (I did end up doing only one side, duplicating that side, flipping it, and putting it on the other side of the star, which worked!), I was stuck for a while figuring out how to fill my star in. I ended up finding how to outline the star through Google AI instead of YouTube, and I used that to show me how to fill it in. (Right now, I'm not sure if the star was supposed to auto-fill or if I was supposed to do it manually, but I ended up doing it manually. Here is my unfilled star:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/af74d87309851c25daafc4d7387b1c25e6259ddc9f3e9b96fad2232dc4e80bc1.png)

I had a LOT of trouble figuring out how to fill the star in. I had to spend almost 30 minutes on that alone. I did a test run with a regular rectangle to see if it was my fault for not connecting some aspects of the star outline or an error on KiCad's end. I was so confused because even using a preexisting rectangle template as a test run, it still wasn't filling in.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/cf1b38f9afbf16feb093f5132776c97ea59926ae5c1b9f7c40639df4346c3ff8.png)

I began to troubleshoot with AI to see what would happen.
I ended up not being able to figure out why my star wasn't filling in. I consulted YouTube, AI, and even the Slack, yet got no response. I decided to move on without it and continue.

Routing the PCB was confusing. I wasn't sure if the red lines were supposed to be slightly off the blue lines, and I had no idea what "golden pad" meant as stated in the guide. My red lines ended up being off from my blue lines. I didn't read the part where I was supposed to switch from F.Cu to B.Cu, and everything became a huge mess with my red lines. I had no idea where I was supposed to add my blue lines, either, and was already exhausted from the star custom boundary not working. Attached below is an image of my mess of red routing lines: (I couldn't even get to the blue ones because everything was such a mess!)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/4de23c0974c2da22bf1f95a57e3c556925594faeb4512b965cb6f1eda1cdd009.png)

Finally, I installed Arduino and completed steps 1-6 of the Upload with Arduino IDE guide! On step 4 though, I accidentally clicked "Install without dependencies" instead of "Install all" when downloading each of the 4 libraries. But it wasn't a problem because I just went back and removed each library, and redownloaded them, pressing "Install all" this time! Here is my step 6 screenshot (I did steps 1-6 too!)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/e3b518fa2abfb6de00bb6de61c3a00ab28530bae6883f081cadd89518809251f.png)

All in all, today, I struggled a lot with a lot of minor functions that ate up all my time. Nevertheless, I learned a lot about perseverance, and I'm excited for my next steps!!

### 2026-10-11 – Today was a pretty unique day in terms of work!

**3.5h**

Today was a pretty unique day in terms of work!
 I just filmed my 5-hour progress reel, which was interesting!
As I write this, I'm starting the final phase of my project, as I just finished my PCB and Schematic Editor. I'm going to finish everything to do with Arduino, and the Next Steps customization.

Just did Customization on my PCB board! I liked how the Starbie looks like a pixelated star, as well as the navy blue background looking like outer space, with the little white grid-points in the background looking like little scattered stars in the sky (I've mentioned that before, haha).
To keep this space-aesthetic up, I decided to add a planet, a moon, and a constellation as my art customizations through Image Converter! An image of my final PCB with customizations is in my README, but an image of me messing around with the dimensions, threshold, and output format is below:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/14b71e3b628e06db19c4f7fdad438d0f90f1401ccd201fece172129edfb1c6b5.png)

I already completed steps 1-5 of the Firmware section on my Mac last night. I tried to finish up the process on my device and do step 6, but I didn't realize that I didn't need to click "Upload" on Starbie.ino because I don't have my physical board yet. So, I tried to click Upload multiple times, and it told me that I don't have enough storage to do so. I deleted a bunch of files and things that were taking up storage on my Mac, but I STILL didn't have enough storage. (AI: Google Gemini was telling me that I needed to download Xcode to Upload on Arduino). The error message is displayed below:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/863c6044cd8d9a392fd72dc6b0ba629d299eb67937daea0c6a801461ff5bd4cc.png)

After messing around with that (and NOT wanting to delete my precious attachments from my Messages app...) for a LONG time, I decided to switch devices over to my PC, which has a LOT more storage than my Mac. Only later did I realize that I didn't have to click Upload anyways... but it's a happy mistake, as I've realized that it's much easier to do this software stuff on a Windows PC anyways. (I'm going to be continuing my work on Half-Life on my PC from now on, haha!)

Starting to work on the customizations to the Arduino code; I'll list them here as I go along...
- I had to change up my code for the wiring because it was different than the guide's; I plugged wires into different pins
- I did connect a temperature sensor (DHT11), so I didn't need to change that
- I wanted to change the pet's starting stats to make them higher. I made the starting joy 80, starting energy 90, and starting fullness 70!
- I liked the preset reactions and their settings; I kept those.
- I followed the guide to add the special effect!
Here's some of my code customizations:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/3470e8345992bb0097770c4b2275dd2598ba0b6411da641174e7b9bff9f12a0a.png)

I did get a little confused on the 32x32 bitmap pet step (the last step); I was a little unsure if I was supposed to draw a sprite or just look one up. I ended up using Pinterest to find a black cat sprite. I had a lot of issues resizing my image to 32x32 though, because  it kept disappearing! I ended up using another website to resize it. This is an error that came up the first time I "resized" it (it just stayed 500x500, so it's good that I caught the code it outputted looking extremely long!):

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/pwNbc3CZtwBCGJ0ZksWAw7XQQPlAMTId/ae0c8a58bdd5ef9b5344560d8235f420da2e7747b37e2dd45f375d5bc7c84b67.png)

Okay, done with Arduino stuff !!

I added my Gerber files from the PCB editor and Arduino, and added them to my GitHub repository!

Overall, today's day was exhausting, yet rewarding; I had to make a lot of final customizations and solve a lot of minor, complex problems that were blocking me from moving forward, but at least I'm done with all the technicalities! And still, after I finish this entry, I have to add the prices to my Bill of Materials and figure out what exactly each piece is going to be needed for...

I'm really glad I persevered, though, and built my Starbie entirely! (Well, online, at least...) I'm super duper excited for the actual build part of this project in five weeks!
Throughout this grueling 10+ hour journey, I can safely say that I have learned SO much about determination, precision, complex computer libraries, folders, and downloads (and files that are always hiding), as well as learning how to work KiCad (specifically the Schematic Editor, PCB Editor, and Image Converter, which are definitely going to help me in my future robotics ventures) and Arduino! I'm hype for next week's project!
